passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Oh! by the kestrels! I can keep my hands off you no longer; you are too slow and lazy altogether.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Parricide: Oh! might I but become an eagle, who soars in the skies! Oh! might I fly above the azure waves of the barren sea!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Ha! it would seem the news was true; I hear someone coming who talks of wings.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Parricide: Nothing is more charming than to fly; I am bird-mad and fly towards you, for I want
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: to live with you and to obey your laws.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Which laws? The birds have many laws.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Parricide: All of them; but the one that pleases me most is that among the birds it is considered a fine thing to peck and strangle one's father.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Yes, by Zeus! according to us,
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: he who dares to strike his father, while still a chick, is a brave fellow.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Parricide: And therefore I want to dwell here, for I want to strangle my father and inherit his wealth.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: But we have also an ancient law written in the code of the storks, which runs thus,
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: When the stork father has reared his young and has taught them to fly, the young must in their turn support the father.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Parricide: It's hardly worth while coming all this distance to be compelled to keep my father!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: No, no, young friend, since you have come to us with such willingness, I am going to give you these black wings, as though you were an orphan bird; furthermore, some good advice, that I received myself in infancy. Don't strike your father, but take
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: these wings in one hand and these spurs in the other; imagine you have a cock's crest on your head and go and mount guard and fight; live on your pay and respect your father's life. You're a gallant fellow! Very well, then! Fly to Thrace and fight.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Parricide: By Bacchus! You're right; I will follow your counsel.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: It's acting wisely, by Zeus..
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Cinesias: On my light pinions I soar off to Olympus ; in its capricious flight my Muse flutters along the thousand paths of poetry in turn ...
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: This is a fellow will need a whole shipload of wings.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Cinesias: ... and being fearless and vigorous, it is seeking fresh outlet.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Welcome, Cinesias, you lime-wood man! Why have you come here twisting your game leg in circles?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Cinesias: I want to become a bird, a tuneful nightingale.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Enough of that sort of ditty. Tell me what you want.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Cinesias: Give me wings and I will fly into the topmost airs to gather fresh songs in the clouds,
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: in the midst of the vapors and the fleecy snow.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Gather songs in the clouds?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Cinesias: 'Tis on them the whole of our latter-day art depends. The most brilliant dithyrambs are those that flap their wings in empty space and are clothed in mist and dense obscurity.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: To appreciate this, just listen.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Oh! no, no, no!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Cinesias: By Hermes! but indeed you shall.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: I shall travel through thine ethereal empire
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: like a winged bird, who cleaveth space with his long neck ...
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Stop! Way enough!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Cinesias: ... as I soar over the seas, carried by the breath of the winds ...
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: By Zeus! I'll cut your breath short. He picks up a pair of wings and begins trying to stop Cinesias' mouth with them.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Cinesias: ... now rushing along the tracks of Notus, now nearing Boreas
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: across the infinite wastes of the ether.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Ah! old man, that's a pretty and clever idea truly!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: What! are you not delighted to be cleaving the air?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Cinesias: To treat a dithyrambic poet, for whom the tribes dispute with each other, in this style!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Will you stay with us and form a chorus of winged birds as slender as Leotrophides for the Cecropid tribe?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Cinesias: You are making game of me, that's clear; but know that I shall never leave you in peace if I do not have wings wherewith to traverse the air.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: What are these birds with downy feathers, who look so pitiable to me? Tell me, oh swallow with the long dappled wings.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Oh! it's a regular invasion that threatens us. Here comes another one, humming along.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: Swallow with the long dappled wings, once more I summon you.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: It's his cloak I believe he's addressing; it stands in great need of the swallows' return.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: Where is he who gives out wings to all comers?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Here I am, but you must tell me for what purpose you want them.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: Ask no questions. I want wings, and wings I must have.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Do you want to fly straight to Pellene ?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: I? Why, I am an accuser of the islands, an informer ...
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: A fine trade, truly!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: ... a hatcher of lawsuits. Hence I have great need of wings
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: to prowl round the cities and drag them before justice.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Would you do this better if you had wings?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: No, but I should no longer fear the pirates; I should return with the cranes, loaded with a supply of lawsuits by way of ballast.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: So it seems, despite all your youthful vigor, you make it your trade to denounce strangers?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: Well, and why not? I don't know how to dig.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: But, by Zeus! there are
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: honest ways of gaining a living at your age without all this infamous trickery.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: My friend, I am asking you for wings, not for words.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: It's just my words that gives you wings.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: And how can you give a man wings with your words?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: They all start this way.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: How?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Have you not often heard
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: the father say to young men in the barbers' shops, It's astonishing how Diitrephes' advice has made my son fly to horse-riding. — Mine, says another, has
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: flown towards tragic poetry on the wings of his imagination.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: So that words give wings?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Undoubtedly; words give wings to the mind and make a man soar to heaven. Thus I hope that my wise words will give you wings
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: to fly to some less degrading trade.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: But I do not want to.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: What do you reckon on doing then?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: I won't belie my breeding; from generation to generation we have lived by informing. Quick, therefore, give me quickly some light, swift hawk or kestrel wings,
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: so that I may summon the islanders, sustain the accusation here, and haste back there again on flying pinions.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: I see. In this way the stranger will be condemned even before he appears.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: That's just it.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: And while he is on his way here by sea, you will be flying to the islands
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: to despoil him of his property.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: You've hit it, precisely; I must whirl hither and thither like a perfect humming-top.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: I catch the idea. Wait, I've got some fine Corcyraean wings. How do you like them?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: Oh! woe is me! Why, it's a whip!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: No, no; these are the wings,
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: I tell you, that make the top spin.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Informer: Oh! oh! oh!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Take your flight, clear off, you miserable cur, or you will soon see what comes of quibbling and lying. The Informer flees. To his slaves. Come, let us gather up our wings and withdraw.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Chorus: In my ethereal flights I have seen many things new and strange and wondrous beyond belief.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: There is a tree called Cleonymus belonging to an unknown species; it has no heart, is good for nothing and is as tall as it is cowardly. In springtime it shoots forth calumnies instead of buds and
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: in autumn it strews the ground with bucklers in place of leaves.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Far away in the regions of darkness, where no ray of light ever enters, there is a country,
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: where men sit at the table of the heroes and dwell with them always —except in the evening.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Should any mortal meet the hero Orestes at night, he would soon be stripped and covered with blows from head to foot.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: Ah! by the gods! if only Zeus does not see me!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Where is Pisthetaerus?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Ha! what is this? A masked man!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: Can you see any god behind me?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: No, none. But who are you, pray?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: What's the time, please?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: The time? Why, it's past noon.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Who are you?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: Is it the fall of day? Is it no later than that?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: This is getting dull!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: What is Zeus doing? Is he dispersing the clouds or gathering them?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Watch out for yourself!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: Come, I will raise my mask.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Ah! my dear Prometheus!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: Sh! Sh! speak lower!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Why, what's the matter, Prometheus?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: Sh! sh! Don't call me by my name; you will be my ruin, if Zeus should see me here. But, if you want me to tell you how things are going in heaven, take this umbrella and shield me, so that the gods don't see me.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: I can recognize Prometheus in this cunning trick. Come, quick then, and fear nothing; speak on.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: Then listen.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: I am listening, proceed!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: Zeus is done for.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Ah! and since when, pray?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: Since you founded this city in the air. There is not a man who now sacrifices to the gods; the smoke of the victims no longer reaches us. Not the smallest offering comes! We fast as though it were the festival of Demeter.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: The barbarian gods, who are dying of hunger, are bawling like Illyrians and threaten to make an armed descent upon Zeus, if he does not open markets where joints of the victims are sold.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: What! there are other gods besides you, barbarian gods who dwell above Olympus ?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: If there were no barbarian gods, who would be the patron of Execestides?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: And what is the name of these gods?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: Their name? Why, the Triballi.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Ah, indeed!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: 'tis from that no doubt that we derive the word ‘tribulation.'
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: Most likely. But one thing I can tell you for certain, namely, that Zeus and the celestial Triballi are going to send deputies here to sue for peace. Now don't you treat with them, unless
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Zeus restores the scepter to the birds and gives you Basileia in marriage.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Who is this Basileia?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: A very fine young damsel, who makes the lightning for Zeus; all things come from her,
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: wisdom, good laws, virtue, the fleet, calumnies, the public paymaster and the triobolus.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Ah! then she is a sort of general manageress to the god.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: Yes, precisely. If he gives you her for your wife, yours will be the almighty power. That is what I have come to tell you;
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: for you know my constant and habitual goodwill towards men.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Oh, yes! it's thanks to you that we roast our meat.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: I hate the gods, as you know.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Aye, by Zeus, you have always detested them.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Prometheus: Towards them I am a veritable Timon; but I must return in all haste,
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: so give me the umbrella; if Zeus should see me from up there, he would think I was escorting one of the Canephori.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Wait, take this stool as well. Prometheus leaves. Pisthetaerus goes into the thicket.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Chorus: Near by the land of the Sciapodes there is a marsh, from the borders whereof the unwashed
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Socrates evokes the souls of men. Pisander came one day to see his soul, which he had left there when still alive. He offered
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: a little victim, a camel, slit his throat and, following the example of Odysseus, stepped one pace backwards. Then that bat of a Chaerephon came up from hell to drink the camel's blood.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: This is the city of Nephelococcygia, to which we come as ambassadors. To Triballus. Hi! what are you up to? you are throwing your cloak over the left shoulder. Come, fling it quick over the right! And why, pray, does it draggle in this fashion? Have you ulcers to hide like Lespodias?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Oh! democracy! whither, oh! whither are you leading us? Is it possible that the gods have chosen such an envoy?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: You are undisturbed?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Ugh! you cursed savage! you are by far the most barbarous of all the gods. —
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Tell me, Heracles, what are we going to do?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: I have already told you
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: that I want to strangle the fellow who dared to wall us out.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: But, my friend, we are envoys of peace.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: All the more reason why I wish to strangle him.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Hand me the cheese-grater; bring me the silphium for sauce;
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: pass me the cheese and watch the coals.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: Mortal! we who greet you are three gods.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Wait a bit till I have prepared my silphium pickle.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: What are these meats?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: These are birds that have been punished with death
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: for attacking the people's friends.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: And you are going to season them before answering us?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Ah! Heracles! welcome, welcome! What's the matter?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: The gods have sent us here as ambassadors to treat for peace.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: There's no more oil in the flask.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: And yet the birds must be thoroughly basted with it.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: We have no interest to serve in fighting you; as for you, be friends and we promise that you shall always have rain-water in your pools and the warmest of warm weather.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: So far as these points go we are plenipotentiaries.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: We have never been the aggressors, and even now we are as well disposed for peace as yourselves, provided you agree to one equitable condition, namely,
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: that Zeus yield his scepter to the birds. If only this is agreed to, I invite the ambassadors to dinner.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: That's good enough for me. I vote for peace.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: You wretch! you are nothing but a fool and a glutton.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Do you want to dethrone your own father?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: What an error. Why, the gods will be much more powerful if the birds govern the earth. At present the mortals are hidden beneath the clouds, escape your observation, and commit perjury in your name;
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: but if you had the birds for your allies, and a man, after having sworn by the crow and Zeus, should fail to keep his oath, the crow would dive down upon him unawares and pluck out his eye.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: Well thought of, by Poseidon!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: My notion too.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: And you, what's your opinion?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Triballus: Nabasatreu.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: D'you see? he also approves. But listen, here is another thing in which we can serve you. If a man vows to offer a sacrifice to some god, and then procrastinates,
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: pretending that the gods can wait, and thus does not keep his word, we shall punish his stinginess.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: Ah! and how?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: While he is counting his money or is in the bath, a kite will relieve him, before he knows it, either in coin or in clothes,
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: of the value of a couple of sheep, and carry it to the god.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: I vote for restoring them the scepter.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: Ask Triballus.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: Hi! Triballus, do you want a thrashing?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Triballus: Sure, bashum head withum stick.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: He says, Right willingly.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: If that be the opinion of both of you, why, I consent too.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: Very well! we accord you the scepter.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Ah! I was nearly forgetting another condition. I will leave Here to Zeus, but only if the young Basileia
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: is given me in marriage.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: Then you don't want peace. Let us withdraw.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: It matters mighty little to me. Cook, look to the gravy.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: What an odd fellow this Poseidon is! Where are you off to? Are we going to war about a woman?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: What else is there to do?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: What else? Why, conclude peace.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: Oh! you blockhead! do you always want to be fooled? Why, you are seeking your own downfall. If Zeus were to die, after having yielded them the sovereignty, you would be ruined, for you are the heir of
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: all the wealth he will leave behind.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Oh! by the gods! how he is cajoling you. Step aside, that I may have a word with you. Your uncle is getting the better of you, my poor friend.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: The law will not allow you an obolus of the paternal property, for you are a bastard and not a legitimate child.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: I a bastard! What's that you tell me?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Why, certainly; are you not born of a stranger woman? Besides, is not Athena recognized as Zeus' sole heiress? And no daughter would be that, if she had a legitimate brother.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: But what if my father wished to give me his property on his death-bed, even though I be a bastard?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: The law forbids it, and this same Poseidon would be the first to lay claim to his wealth, in virtue of being his legitimate brother. Listen;
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: thus runs Solon's law: A bastard shall not inherit, if there are
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: legitimate children; and if there are no legitimate children, the property shall pass to the nearest kin.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: And I get nothing whatever of the paternal property?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Absolutely nothing. But tell me, has your father had you entered on the registers of his phratry?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: No, and I have long been surprised at the omission.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Why do you shake your fist at heaven? Do you want to fight? Why, be on my side, I will make you a king and will feed you on bird's milk and honey.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: Your further condition seems fair to me.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: I cede you the young damsel.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: But I, I vote against this opinion.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Then it all depends on the Triballus. To the Triballus. What do you say?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Triballus: Givum bird pretty gel bigum queen.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: He says give her.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: Why no, he does not say anything of the sort, or else, like the swallows he does not know how to walk.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Exactly so. Does he not say she must be given to the swallows?
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Poseidon: All right, you two arrange the matter; make peace, since you wish it so; I'll hold my tongue.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: We are of a mind to grant you all that you ask. But come up there with us to receive Basileia and the celestial bounty.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Here are birds already dressed, and very suitable for a nuptial feast.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: You go and, if you like, I will stay here to roast them.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: You to roast them? you are too much the glutton; come along with us.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Heracles: Ah! how well I would have treated myself!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Let some one bring me a beautiful and magnificent tunic for the wedding.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Chorus: At Phanae, near the
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Clepsydra, there dwells a people who have neither faith nor law, the Englottogastors, who reap, sow, pluck the vines and the figs with their tongues;
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: they belong to a barbaric race, and among them the Philippi and the Gorgiases are to be found; 'tis these Englottogastorian Philippi who introduced the custom all over Attica
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: of cutting out the tongue separately at sacrifices.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Messenger: Oh, you, whose unbounded happiness I cannot express in words, thrice happy race of airy birds, receive your king in your fortunate dwellings. More brilliant than the brightest
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: star that illumes the earth, he is approaching his glittering golden palace; the sun itself does not shine with more dazzling glory. He is entering with his bride at his side, whose beauty no human tongue can express; in his hand he brandishes the lightning, the winged shaft of Zeus;
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: perfumes of unspeakable sweetness pervade the ethereal realms. 'Tis a glorious spectacle to see the clouds of incense wafting in light whirlwinds before the breath of the zephyr! But here he is himself. Divine Muse! let thy sacred lips begin with songs of happy omen.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Chorus: Fall back! to the right! to the left! advance! Fly around this happy mortal, whom Fortune loads with her blessings. Oh! oh! what grace! what beauty!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Oh, marriage so auspicious for our city!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: All honor to this man! 'tis through him that the birds are called to such glorious destinies. Let your nuptial hymns, your nuptial songs, greet
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: him and his Basileia!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: 'Twas that the Fates formerly united Olympian Hera to the King who governs the gods from the summit of his inaccessible throne
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: in the midst of such festivities. Oh! Hymen! oh! Hymenaeus!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Rosy Eros with the golden wings held the reins and guided the chariot; 'twas he, who presided over
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: the union of Zeus and the fortunate Hera. Oh! Hymen! oh! Hymenaeus!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: I am delighted with your songs, I applaud your verses. Now celebrate
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: the thunder that shakes the earth, the flaming lightning of Zeus and the terrible flashing thunderbolt.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Chorus: Oh, thou golden flash of the lightning! oh, ye divine shafts of flame, that Zeus has hitherto shot forth!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Oh, ye rolling thunders, that bring down the rain! 'Tis by the order of our king that ye shall now stagger the earth! Oh, Hymen! 'tis through thee that he commands the universe and that he makes Basileia, whom he has robbed from Zeus, take her seat at his side. Oh! Hymen! oh! Hymenaeus!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Pisthetaerus: Let all the winged tribes of our fellow-citizens follow the bridal couple to the palace of Zeus and to the nuptial couch! Stretch forth your
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: hands, my dear wife! Take hold of me by my wings and let us dance; I am going to lift you up and carry you through the air.
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Chorus: Alalalai ie Paian! Tenella kallinikos!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage

passages.text: Loftiest art thou of gods!
passages.locusKind: TEI English line marker; segment not automatically aligned to Greek passage
